Summary: "Attention Is All You Need" is a 2017 research paper authored by eight scientists and engineers working at Google, introducing a new deep learning architecture known as the transformer. The paper was presented at the 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017) and proposed a novel network architecture based solely on an attention mechanism, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. The authors are Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, and Illia Polosukhin. The paper's model combines multi-head self-attention with a position-wise feed-forward layer in both the encoder and decoder.

Summary: The 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" introduced the Transformer architecture, which relies entirely on attention mechanisms to draw global dependencies between input and output, replacing recurrent layers. The paper, authored by eight scientists and engineers working at Google, proposed the Transformer model that allows for significantly more parallelization and achieved state-of-the-art translation quality. The Transformer architecture has become the main architecture for a wide variety of artificial intelligence systems, including large language models. The paper's title is a reference to the Beatles' song "All You Need Is Love," and the name "Transformer" was chosen because one of the authors liked the sound of that word.
